content: Do not store this medication in the bathroom, as it should be kept in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When this product is expired or no longer needed, dispose of it properly. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication, commonly known by the brand name Viracept, is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, nelfinavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Before starting nelfinavir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it each time you get a refill. If you have difficulty swallowing tablets, you may crush your dose and take it with food. Alternatively, the tablets can be dissolved in a small amount of water. If dissolved, stir the mixture well and drink it immediately. Rinse the container with additional water and drink the rinse liquid to ensure you receive the full dose. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor. Diarrhea is a common side effect of this medication. If you experience diarrhea, consult your doctor or pharmacist about ways to manage this side effect, such as using anti-diarrheal medication. Nausea or gas may also occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. In rare cases, this medication may cause an increase in blood sugar levels, which can lead to or worsen diabetes. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nelfinavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV infection to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication, as breast milk can also transmit HIV. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Nelfinavir can slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of nelfinavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, certain anti-seizure drugs (such as carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone), and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, lab and/or medical tests (such as liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, and blood sugar) should be performed regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
